parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: 2-methylpropene reacts with $\text{HCl(g)}$ at room temperature. The major organic product is 2-chloro-2-methylpropane.

parts.label: (a)(i)
(a)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why, in this reaction, 2-chloro-2-methylpropane is produced at a higher yield than 1-chloro-2-methylpropane.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem:
Two bottles labelled $\mathbf{Q}$ and $\mathbf{M}$ each contain a straight-chain halogenoalkane with molecular formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{X}$, where $\mathbf{X}$ represents $\text{Cl}$, $\text{Br}$ or $\text{I}$. A sample from each bottle is added to separate samples of equal amounts of aqueous silver nitrate in ethanol. In each reaction, the same organic product, $\mathbf{T}$, and a precipitate are made, as shown in Fig. 4.2.

$$\mathbf{Q} \xrightarrow{\text{AgNO}_3\text{(aq) in ethanol}} \mathbf{T} \xleftarrow{\text{AgNO}_3\text{(aq) in ethanol}} \mathbf{M}$$

Fig. 4.2

Table 4.1 describes the colour of each of the precipitates made.

Table 4.1

| halogenoalkane added to $\text{AgNO}_3\text{(aq)}$ in ethanol | colour of precipitate |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\mathbf{Q}$ | white |
| $\mathbf{M}$ | yellow |

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Identify the functional group present in $\mathbf{T}$ and name the type of reaction that occurs using the information in Fig. 4.2 and Table 4.1.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Construct an ionic equation to describe the formation of the yellow precipitate produced when $\mathbf{M}$ reacts with $\text{AgNO}_3\text{(aq)}$ in ethanol.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Describe which reagent, $\mathbf{Q}$ or $\mathbf{M}$, will produce a precipitate more quickly when each is added to $\text{AgNO}_3\text{(aq)}$ in ethanol. Explain your answer.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text:
When pure $\mathbf{T}$ is added to alkaline $\text{I}_2\text{(aq)}$, a yellow precipitate and an anion, $\mathbf{L}$, are made.

Identify the anion $\mathbf{L}$.

parts.label: (b)(v)
parts.text: Deduce the structure of the straight-chain halogenoalkane $\mathbf{M}$.
